cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component ('Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code demonstrates command injection: user-controlled href is directly substituted into a command template containing %u placeholder, then executed via shell interpreter without neutralization of special shell characters

connection.evidence: href flows from user input (URLs) or editor configuration through string substitution directly to os.execv("/bin/sh", ["/bin/sh", "-c", path]) - clear path from external input to shell execution

diff_causality.evidence: If this line were reverted, the %u placeholder would remain unsubstituted, preventing the injection vulnerability. The substitution is the material change that enables the injection

security_control.evidence: Required control: proper neutralization of special shell characters in user input before shell command construction. Deficiency: href is directly substituted without escaping, quoting, or parameterization. Existing controls checked: encoder() function applied after substitution but purpose unclear, no shell escaping observed
security_control.required_control: shell command parameterization or proper escaping of user input
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-74 requires neutralization when constructing commands for downstream interpreters; shell commands require escaping of metacharacters to prevent injection
existing_controls_checked: encoder() function applied to path after substitution but before execv - purpose unclear from evidence
security_control.deficiency_evidence: href is directly substituted into command template without shell escaping, allowing injection of shell metacharacters

concrete_impact.evidence: Arbitrary command execution is demonstrated through the shell execution path. The consequence depends on attacker-controlled href content but the mechanism supports full command injection

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the %u placeholder would remain in the path string, preventing substitution of user input and thus eliminating the injection vulnerability.
supporting_evidence: href is user-controlled input from URLs or editor configuration
path template contains %u placeholder for substitution
resulting command executed via os.execv("/bin/sh", ["/bin/sh", "-c", path])
No shell escaping or parameterization applied to href before substitution
unresolved_facts: Exact security purpose and effectiveness of encoder() function
Whether browser configuration validation prevents malicious templates
Specific validation applied to href URLs before use
review_comment: User-controlled href is directly substituted into a shell command template without proper escaping, enabling command injection. The substitution replaces %u with href content that may contain shell metacharacters, then executes the resulting command via /bin/sh. Use shell escaping or parameterization (e.g., shlex.quote()) on href before substitution to neutralize special characters.
